scope: Optional xmqtt_client_tls_resume adds one latest native TLS1.3 credential slot and thread-safe Info/Take APIs to the existing TLS client. Existing public Client/TLS configuration and result layouts do not change. Native public APIs already implement ticket/PSK/expiry/peer binding; no Core/runtime or cryptographic implementation change is required.

Native ticket events drain at most the native public64-entry bound, transferring existing immutable references without creating an adapter node or copying credentials/DER. Replacement retains the newest fitting credential, releases the old native reference outside the Client gate and coalesces the existing Client work. Optional local quota refusal preserves an older credential and the healthy connection.

Capture/Evicted/Rejected counters describe actual native-object handoffs to the adapter and saturate. They do not count native disabled/full/OOM drops. Native ResumeLimit0 and native mutual authentication disable capture. The native client currently supports TLS1.3 credential publication/resumption; TLS1.2 full handshakes continue unchanged.

Established/Resumed describe authenticated TLS, independently of MQTT readiness. Each new connection still performs CONNECT/CONNACK/authentication and has fresh protocol state. Native ResumeOnly controls full-handshake fallback. This does not implement reconnect, MQTT durable session recovery, automatic cross-connection cache management or 0-RTT/request replay.

Take transfers the sole cached native reference with no allocation/copy/post and refunds local cache data-byte credit. Empty preserves output/error. Any thread may take with a stable borrowed Client, including Notify and after ClientWait. The credential can outlive Client/Engine; its caller owns storage/budget and retains Core code until final release. A new factory retains it before DNS. Secret/ticket contents are never recorded in evidence.
resource_contract: MaxPrivateBytes charges the selected fixed TLS state and cached ticket/PSK/identity/name/ALPN bytes plus saved peer-chain DER. Native opaque credential metadata, shared parsed-chain allocation and bounded native queue remain separately governed by Core policy/verification limits outside this local data-byte accounting; this is not an RSS or exact native allocation-size claim. Taking a credential transfers its budget responsibility to the new caller.

The optional module adds no adapter allocation per ticket. Capturing performs native metadata/peer-certificate getters, O(chain count) size summation, one Client-gate update per taken credential, immutable-reference release and a coalesced wake. The notification flag is sampled in the existing Work-entry gate; no extra steady-state mutex or Work item is introduced. Native ticket creation, parsing, certificate/crypto operations and shared-reference costs remain real.

Measured layouts, allocation counters, setup timing and before/off/compiled steady-state TLS data comparisons are retained per OS below. Public TLS config200, ClientConfig272, Info160 and request header104 are required unchanged; the new resume-info and selected private-state sizes are measured rather than inferred.
